packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-13 — unverified image reading (UTF-8 plain text)
Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this record. I opened only the brief, PROMPT.md, and the packet's image files (plus a sips size listing of those images to tell overviews from tiles).

LAYOUT SURVEY (face 1, overview image-001.jpg, reduced)
- One plate holding several separate paper fragments, each with a modern pencil shelfmark label "Stams, STA, Fag. 176-1r", "-2r", "-3r", "-4r", "-5r". Colour checker and ruler present. Some grey rectangles are digital masks over areas of the images (not damage).
- 176-1r (left, tall narrow strip): German cursive (Kurrent-type) hand, ~8 lines at top, enlarged flourished initial at line 1 ("D..."?). A vertical fold/line runs down the strip (text crosses it). Then a short 3-line block below ("Von der Obrigkeit ... Stams ... am 7 tag ... "), apparently a dating/closing clause. Rest of strip blank. Observation: looks like a document heading or endorsement, not a book page.
- 176-2r (centre strip): German cursive, account-style entries, each paragraph ending in a sum written right-justified after a long dash ("76 fl 22", "4 fl 48?", "8 fl 31 k"). Three entries visible; lower part blank.
- 176-3r (right strip): mostly blank; a 5-line block mid-strip ("Gerichts...", ...) ending with a numeral "15"? above a horizontal rule.
- 176-4r (horizontal strip, lower centre, in two pieces joined, with transparent tape-like repair across): Latin text, smaller formal hand, 4-5 lines; "Ord[in]atio(?)" written as a heading at top-centre; "B. Hermannus ..." visible at line start. Distinct from the German pieces.
- 176-5r (small strip at bottom): no visible text in the overview except the pencil label.
- Tiles: images 002-017 appear to be a 4x4 native-resolution grid of this face (rows: 002-005, 006-009, 010-013, 014-017). Image-018 is the overview of face 2 (tiles 019-034). Images 035-036 are small separate images (not yet viewed at survey time).

READINGS (by tile; line numbers counted from top of each image)

--- image-002.jpg (tile row 1, col 1: top of fragment 176-1r; text cut at right edge, continues in image-003) ---
German cursive; large looped initial at top-left spanning lines 1-2. Paper fold/crease runs vertically through the text (left of centre) and a second one near the right edge. Text block (all lines truncated at right edge of tile):
002.01  D[initial] swalthen(?) Streyler(?) [cut]
002.02  Pauel(?) Brut(?) sohne(?) [cut]   (overview shows "...Brut ...ne al[s]")
002.03  Gerhabere(?) vnnd Pe[cut]
002.04  Brutschen(?) vnd sein[cut]   (macron/stroke over "vnd"?)
002.05  gebruoder(?) Raithun[g?][cut]
002.06  vollennd(?) lanns(?) [cut]
002.07  Zu(?) Ständach(?) seligen(?) [cut]
002.08  lassen(?) Khinder ob[cut]   ("lassen" possibly "[ver]lassen" continuing previous line)
002.09  [blank]
002.10  Von der Obrigkhait [cut]   (flourished V with large loop)
002.11  Stambs(?) am 7 tag [cut]
002.12  Marty(?) a[nno] 15(?)95 beschl[...](?) [cut]   (date: "7 tag" + month + year ending "95"; first digits uncertain)
Notes: "Gerhaber" = guardian(s) and "Raithung" = account are tentative word readings of the visible letters, not supplied.

--- image-003.jpg (tile row 1, col 2: right half of 176-1r top, overlapping image-002; left edge of 176-2r) ---
176-1r line endings (same lines as 002.01-12; overlap, not new lines; given as the continuation of each line):
003 ~ 002.01  ...Streyler(?) auch(?)
003 ~ 002.02  ...[Bru]t sohne al[s]
003 ~ 002.03  ...vnnd Pet[er](?) (abbreviation stroke after "Pet")
003 ~ 002.04  ...[v]nd seine(?)   ("seine" with final stroke; could be "seine[n]")
003 ~ 002.05  ...Raithung
003 ~ 002.06  ...lanns(?) gewesen(?)   (word ends with long flourish; "gewesen" tentative)
003 ~ 002.07  ...seligen ver
003 ~ 002.08  ...[Kh]inder ob[...]tr[...](?)   (word partly obscured by a hole/ink blot; possibly "Obtragsch.." [illegible])
003 ~ 002.10  ...[Obrigk]heit [-]ge(?)  (very short ending, unclear)
003 ~ 002.11  ...tag
003 ~ 002.12  ...beschch(?)   (reads like "beschehen" abbreviated, uncertain)
Right edge of 176-1r: blank, damaged, insect/loss holes; no further text.
176-2r left edges visible at right of tile: "Also bl[...]", "Den K[...]", "Nit a[...]"; "Hat [...]", "D[...]", "75 [...]", "baus[...]", "wegen(?)" — read fully in image-004.

--- image-004.jpg (tile row 1, col 3: fragment 176-2r upper part; left letters cut — see image-003 right edge) ---
Account entries; sums right-aligned after a long flourished dash. "fl" written as a looped ff-like sign (= florin/gulden sign, kept as "fl").
004.01  [A]lso bleiben die Brutschen   (the "B" is a large looped capital)
004.02  den Kindern vätterlichs   (umlaut-like marks over "a"; "vätterlich[s]" tentative)
004.03  nit noch schuldig(?)
004.04                                — 76 fl 22
004.05  [blank]
004.06  Hat Peter Brutsch an   (or "Brutsch[en]"; final letters "ch an" uncertain)
004.07  Ubernommen(?)[...]ess(?) d[...]o(?)   (word with D/U-loop initial; "Vbernommenes"? uncertain; tail cut at edge)
004.08  75 [?] vom Andre(?) [K]la[...]   ("75" followed by a bracket/abbrev sign; name uncertain)
004.09  baus(?)chadl(?) von d[en](?) Kinder   ("d" with abbreviation stroke)
004.10  wegen eingenomen(?)   ("ein-" written closely, possibly "endthanung"? reading insecure)
004.11                                — 4 fl 48 7(?)   (third numeral group "48" then "7" or "k"? reads "4 fl 48 7"; overview gave "4 fl 48 7")
004.12  [blank]
004.13  Mer(?) het er vom Osw(?)alde[n] [...]   (bottom line, cut; continues in image-008)

--- image-008.jpg (tile row 2, col 3: 176-2r middle; top line overlaps 004.11) ---
008.01  [overlap = 004.11]  — 4 fl 48 7   (here clearly "4 fl 487" or "4 fl 48 7")
008.02  [blank]
008.03  Mer het er vom Oswalde[n](?)   (first letter a small M/W-like form with flourish)
008.04  [S]trobl(?) als Gerhaben dur[ch](?)   (name before "als": "Strobl"/"Kriebl"? uncertain; "Gerhaben" with looped G)
008.05  verwunde(?) hab ein[...]ganng(?)   (same final word-shape as 004.10; possibly "einnemung"/"empfanng"; uncertain)
008.06                                — 8 fl 31 k
Below: blank paper with a grey digital mask; right edge torn. No further text on 176-2r.

--- image-009.jpg (tile row 2, col 4: fragment 176-3r middle; text block lower half of tile; right edge torn so line ends lost) ---
009.01  Hanndlung(?) [...]   (looped H; mark above "u"/"n"; last letters "-ng" or "-ngs" before loss)
009.02  Zwischen(?) [hole] ke[...](?)   (hole in paper after first word)
009.03  Christls(?) [...]ira(?)[...]   ("Christl" with looped C; following word "pira"/"seira"? uncertain)
009.04  [..]rischtg(?) vnd bra[...]   (first word uncertain; "vnd" clear)
009.05  Verlassenschaften(?)   ("Verla[ss]enschaft[en]": "Verla" clear, long-s ligature, then "-nschafte(n)" tentative)
009.06  [flourished stroke] 15[...]   (numerals "1 5" with dot over 1, rest lost/blank?)
Below: horizontal rule (seen in overview). Everything above this block on the tile is blank paper.
Interpretation (tentative): an endorsement/docket naming a transaction concerning an estate ("Verlassenschaft"), not continuous text.

--- image-015.jpg (tile row 4, col 2: left part of Latin strip 176-4r, two pieces; text begins ~60% across the tile; lines cut at right edge, continue in image-016) ---
Hand: small upright cursive/humanistic-looking Latin hand with some Kurrent-like forms; numbered items ("3.", "4.") at line starts. Transparent tape repair along the join between the two pieces (seam crosses line 3 of upper piece).
Upper piece:
015.u1  B. Hermanns(?) M[cut]   ("B." with looped capital; "Hermann[u]s" final -s or -us sign)
015.u2  Caro(?) Jesus(?) [cut]   (first word "Caro"/"Cara"? second "Jesus" with long-s)
015.u3  S[...] [...]imme(?)[cut]   (mostly under/at the tape seam; [illegible] at start)
Lower piece:
015.l1  Videt dæmon[cut]   (first letter V/U looped; "dæmon" with abbreviation?)
015.l2  3. Qui instru[cut]   (circumflex-like mark over "i" of "Qui")
015.l3  dignis fugam(?) [cut]   (line begins further left than the others; "fugam" or "fuga[n]t" uncertain; mark above)
015.l4  4. Monachus [cut]   (a long dark stroke — a crack or line — runs diagonally across this word)

--- image-016.jpg (tile row 4, col 3: centre of Latin strip 176-4r; overlaps 015 at left; lines cut at right, continue in image-017) ---
Heading line above text, centred: 
016.h   Ordinctio(?) [...]   (reads "Ordinctio"/"Ordinatio"; followed by a short abbreviation, "1?"/"&c"; a small paper loss and tape at the top edge; modern pencil label "Stams, STA, Fag. 1[76-4r]" at right — modern, not text)
Upper piece (each line = continuation of 015.u1-u3):
